newsitem.title: USA: US core inflation "well behaved" - Labor economist.
newsitem.headline: US core inflation "well behaved" - Labor economist.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department Economist Patrick Jackman said Thursday U.S. core inflation remains "well behaved" and the higher than expected rise in the April core rate was influenced by an early Easter holiday.

Jackman told Reuters Financial Television that clothing sales usually associated with the Easter holiday were earlier than usual this year because the holiday occurred at the end of March rather than in April.
As a result, clothing prices returned to regular price levels in April, which influenced the core rate of inflation, which excludes volatile energy and food prices.
Jackman said that the return to regular price levels for clothes does not necessarily mean consumers are more willing to pay full price and not waiting for sales.
"It's a little early in the year for sales, except the promotional Easter sales," Jackman said.
"It's basically a timing issue here and there is really no price pressure in the apparel area," Jackman said.

The Labor Department reported on Thursday that the Consumer Price Index rose a modest 0.1 percent in April, while the core rate rose by 0.3 percent, slightly higher than the 0.2 percent expected by many financial analysts.
Apparel costs jumped 0.9 percent last month after falling 0.3 percent in March, the department said.
Jackman said that inflation trends are well behaved.
"The core remains well behaved," Jackman said.
He said he saw nothing on the short-term horizon to move the U.S. inflation rate from its recent pattern.
